svg.aria-label: Three columns. Left: the Rust source, one helper of each inline kind plus a const-generic device helper. Middle: the request recorded on mir.func as a typed attribute and lowered to the LLVM function attribute, shown on the real define lines, and the one request that is not carried. Right: the PTX, with a real call for each noinline helper, the const-generic factor folded to an immediate, no function left for the alwaysinline helper, and what main did before. A bottom strip explains the libNVVM shared-pointer-return legalization.

text.style: font: 600 17px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: An inline request now reaches the GPU as the matching LLVM attribute

text.style: font: 400 12.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--muted); white-space: pre

svg.text: Only #[inline(always)] used to survive. Now #[inline] is inlinehint, #[inline(always)] is alwaysinline and #[inline(never)] is noinline, as in rustc's own backend, so a never helper stays a real PTX function.

svg.text: The libNVVM route needed one more piece (nvvm-transforms, legalize_pointer_returns)

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: A noinline helper that returns a shared-memory pointer is now a real function. libNVVM declares that 32-bit return slot as .param .b64 while the body stores 32 bits and the call site reads 32,

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: so ptxas rejected addressof_sharedarray on --emit-nvvm-ir. The pass gives such a definition a generic pointer return and an addrspacecast on both sides of each call; parameters, aggregates,

text.style: font: 400 11.5px var(--sans); fill: var(--fg); white-space: pre

svg.text: kernels and declarations are untouched, and a function whose address is taken is reported. The libNVVM defect is tracked with its team; the pass goes when the fix ships.
